newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar expected to be range-bound in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar expected to be range-bound in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be range-bound against the yen in Asia on Thursday, with trade likely to be sandwiched between persistent buying interest from Japanese investors on the downside and lingering concern about Bank of Japan (BOJ) dollar-sellling intervention on the topside, dealers said.
Comments from Japanese and U.S. authorities on Wednesday will still have an impact and fuel intervention fears in Asia, weighing on the dollar, they added.
The market is awaiting the release of both Japanese and U.S. trade data due later in the day.

Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Ministry of Finance's International Finance Bureau, said on Wednesday that recent movements of the yen were clearly excessive, and that Japanese authorities will intervene in foreign exchange markets when appropriate and when they see that it can be effective, saying: "We will intervene when we think we can win."
But he did not elaborate on whether the authorities were willing to intervene now.
"His comments made clear that Japan is ready to intervene any time," a trust bank dealer said, adding that the dollar's advance is likely to be capped around 126.50 yen.
In addition to Sakakibara's comments, remarks by U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky also weighed on the dollar against the yen overnight.

In Washington, Barshefsky said on Wednesday that the United States was concerned about its trade imbalance with Japan and that Washington did not wish to see the gap grow wider, adding that she expected it to be a topic at a meeting between President Bill Clinton and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto next week.
Dealers said steady buying interest from Japanese investors on dips will support the dollar despite intervention fears.
"On the back of the U.S.-Japan interest rate gap, institutional investors' demand for dollar buying in connection with their overseas investments is strong," a city bank dealer said.
The trust bank dealer said the dollar could eventually test the upside because a slew of yen-supportive statements took the dollar down only to around 125.50 yen overnight.
The market is now focusing on Japan's customs-cleared merchandise trade surplus for March due out at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Wednesday) and U.S. international trade figures for February at 1230 GMT.
